summary.headline: BEML Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% with Rail and Metro up 178%, and management guides to similar growth each quarter and around 13% EBITDA for FY27.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 was the best first quarter in roughly a decade, with top-line growth of 29%, Rail and Metro up 178%, Defence up 25% and Mining & Construction (HEMM) down 14%. Management said Q1 was the first positive EBITDA quarter in company history and the loss roughly halved, though no absolute figures were given on the call. Order book is about INR16,000 crore, with an export order book of about USD115 million targeted to reach about USD200 million by year-end. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in the high 20s percent, EBITDA margin back to at least 13%, and order inflow of about INR20,000 crore. Forex losses booked in Q4 are expected to be mitigated to 20-25% in FY27 as foreign-currency contracts are executed.

Contract finalisation deferred on projects where BEML is L1

financial_highlights.value: Positive for the first time (Q1), no figure disclosed

Expected to reach around USD200 million by year-end
Management said it was hit by a one-off correction

segments.name: Rail and Metro
segments.commentary: Revenue up 178% YoY in Q1 FY27 and now 65% of the order book. About 20-25 Bangalore Metro trains expected to be supplied this year after CRS inspection; 16 trainsets bid for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed corridor (B28).

segments.name: Defence and Aerospace
segments.commentary: Revenue up 25% YoY in Q1 FY27 and about 25% of the order book. Management sees about INR4,000-5,000 crore of defence orders this year, including about INR600-700 crore for QRSAM supporting vessels; a 48-unit LCH fuselage order from HAL was received.

segments.name: Mining and Construction (HEMM)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 14% YoY in Q1 FY27 as L1 contract finalisation was deferred; about 4% of the order book. Two Coal India subsidiary orders were received in the current month, and about INR900 crore of L1 tenders are pending.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 6% of the order book, with about 35% of this year's order inflow to date coming from exports. Two export opportunities in Metro worth about INR15,000 crore are being worked on, plus a West Asia HEMM opportunity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected in the high 20s percent, with similar growth (around 29%) each quarter.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to return to at least 13%, versus 13-13.3% in FY25 that was affected by a one-off correction.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR20,000 crore, with a 30-40% probability per management; mix about 65-70% Rail and Metro, about 20% Defence, about 5% international and 5-6% mining.
Forex losses booked in Q4 FY26 expected to be reduced to 20-25% in FY27 and more in later years as foreign-currency contracts are executed; management said there will be no adverse impact.
Long-term mix aspiration of 65-70% Rail and Metro plus Defence and 30% HEMM; Defence could reach 50% of revenue while Rail falls to about 20%.
Medium-term aim of 20% revenue CAGR, EBITDA margin of at least 17-18%, and lower working capital, debtors and inventory.
capex_capacity: Bhopal new plant: construction not yet started; boundary wall done; civil tender to be finalised in 2-3 months; debt financing being arranged; 18 months from construction start to first equipment, about 24 months to complete.
Aditya high-speed train complex: about INR250 crore invested, fully operational; HSR bulk production to follow.

Capex plan: about INR600-plus crore this year, then about INR900 crore for Brahma spread over the next 2-3 years; Chhattisgarh (Mungeli, near Bilaspur, about 80 acres) capex to be worked out in 3-4 months, with a 4-5 year total capex plan.

Bilaspur hub is largely built and will be used for wheeled mining equipment and spares/service hub-and-spoke model; Mysore land (about 300 acres on lease) for aerospace, capex not yet formulated; Bengaluru (36 acres) already producing LHB coaches, with capex of about INR3-4 crore.
Rail and Metro capacity target of 350-400 units unchanged from prior 250-unit base, per management.
demand_pricing: Rail and Metro pipeline: six live Metro tenders (Chennai Metro, Delhi Metro RS20 and RS21, UP Metro extension, Pune-Nagpur Maha Metro, MMRDA Line 12 where BEML bid); MRVC tender reportedly cancelled; MEMU still alive.
Export Metro opportunities of about INR15,000 crore in two countries (not named).

Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR: two prototype 280 kmph trains mandated; 16-trainset offer submitted; management sees about 600 trains across seven future corridors, with about 50% share potentially open to BEML and two suppliers expected in total.

Defence pipeline: ARV WZT-3 overhaul, command post vehicle, self-propelled mine barrier, tank transporters, Light Armoured Multi-purpose Vehicle (winter trials next), and DAC-cleared 230 units; Pinaka excluded from the order estimate.

HEMM: L1 positions in several tenders; cutter suction dredger offer submitted with ordering expected in 2-3 months; export HEMM orders expected in 2-3 months from Middle East. About 80% of mining equipment goes to Coal India and subsidiaries.
Management said sustenance (spares and services) carries the highest margin, with exports close behind.

qa_highlights.question: Why were leased land parcels (Mysore 300 acres, Bengaluru 36 acres) taken back from BEML Land Assets, and for how long?
qa_highlights.answer: Land lies unused and is leased at a small rental for production: Bengaluru is already producing LHB coaches and Mysore is for aerospace (LCH fuselage order). The 99-year lease will be reviewed after five years or earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Has the MRVC tender been cancelled, and what is the INR40,000 crore pipeline composed of?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MRVC was cancelled. The INR20,000 crore Rail and Metro pipeline (six Metro tenders, two export opportunities, the B28 HSR bid, and MEMU) plus about INR4,000-5,000 crore defence, INR900 crore L1 mining and INR500-600 crore additional mining bids.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 revenue growth and EBITDA margin expectations, and what is the forex impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth in the high 20s percent; EBITDA margin at least 13%. Management expects the Q4 forex loss to be cut to 20-25% in FY27 as foreign-currency contracts are realised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bhopal plant timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction has not started; civil tender to be finalised in 2-3 months and debt funding being arranged. Plant to roll out first equipment 18 months after construction begins; full completion in about 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment mix outlook and order book break-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Long term 65-70% Rail and Metro plus Defence, 30% HEMM. Current order book: 65% Rail and Metro, 25% Defence, 4% Mining, 6% Exports. FY27 order inflow to date INR1,181 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: what steps are being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue skew (about 10%/20%/30%/40% by quarter, with Q4 about 45% last year) drives debtors up; plan is an executable order pipeline at start of year and about 35% revenue by Q2 and 70% by Q3 to reduce the Q4 spike and inventory.

risks_watch: Realisation of the INR20,000 crore order inflow target, which management put at a 30-40% probability.
Mining and Construction slowdown from deferred L1 contract finalisation; HEMM revenue fell 14% YoY in Q1.
Working capital and debtor build-up from the Q4-heavy revenue skew; the H1 and Q3 revenue targets are key to the plan.
Bhopal and Chhattisgarh capex funding; debt financing for Bhopal not yet secured.
HSR timeline: prototype trains due in about 4-5 months, with testing extending into the following year; no cost-per-coach figure given.
Realisation of forex loss mitigation as foreign-currency contracts are executed.
The export order book target of USD200 million by year-end, and the dependence on 2-3 month ordering timelines for cutter suction dredgers and export HEMM.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on FY27 growth and Rail and Metro, with specific numeric guidance. Evasive on HSR cost per coach, Mysore capex, marine and TBM programmes, and the defence-to-50% question, which management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: The last quarter has been quite an improvement, probably the best first quarter we have had in the last decade or so with a top line growth of 29%.
The first time probably again we have hit a positive EBITDA ever and the overall loss has gone down by almost 50%.
So overall CAGR should be I mean for this year, it should be high 20s if all goes well and it should go well because we have the executable orders now
My guess is that the losses that we have already booked, it will get mitigated to at least 20%-25% in this financial year and maybe more in the coming years.
So it will help in bringing the debtors under control to a great extent.
